newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-MORRIS REACHES GLAMORGAN SCORING LANDMARK.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-MORRIS REACHES GLAMORGAN SCORING LANDMARK.

text.p: Glamorgan and former England opener Hugh Morris struck an unbeaten 158 to become the fourth-highest run scorer in his county's history on Thursday.
Morris spurred his team to 319 for three at the close on the second day of the rain-hit county championship match against Gloucestershire at Swansea.
He shared a third-wicket partnership of 223 with his captain Matthew Maynard (98) after the Welsh side slipped to 40 for two.
They only took 20 overs to record the 100 partnership before Morris went on to three figures in just over three hours, hitting 12 fours and passing 18,000 first-class runs for the county.
Surrey paceman Martin Bicknell rocked Warwickshire by grabbing their first three wickets for 12 runs in 37 balls at Edgbaston.
Warwickshire slumped to 55 for four in reply to Surrey's first innings of 193, but Dougie Brown led a revival with an unbeaten 57 to steer his side to 159 for four at the close.
Scotsman Brown received valuable support from Trevor Penney (47 not out) in a fifth wicket stand of 104 in 26 overs.
Lancashire took control against leaders Middlesex at Uxbridge, making 309 for four in reply to the home side's meagre first innings of 118.
Neil Fairbrother (82 not out) and Ian Austin (35 not out) consolidated after opener Nathan Wood (67) and Steve Titchard (79) provided a firm foundation.
Lengthy stoppages for rain at Chelmsford failed to prevent Somerset batsmen Mark Lathwell (87) and Piran Holloway (90) achieving their highest scores of the season, against Essex.
Their third-wicket partnership produced 147 and provided the foundation for Somerset's 246 for six in reply to Essex's first innings of 280.
